Small PD challenge study (n=6) corroborated longer levodopa dyskinesia duration with caffeine.
Decaf espresso served only as a somnolence placebo arm; dystonia was not measured.
Incidence cohort (null for decaf coffee) provides no dystonia severity data.
Global MoCA was -0.66 pts worse on caffeine capsules over 6-18 mo, but executive subscores were not reported separately.
PD crossover explicitly demonstrated no selective Stroop inhibitory-control effect (F<1), separating general attention/response selection from executive inhibition.

study: Todorovic et al. 2021 (PMID:34532023), Cornelis et al. 2020 (PMID:32495843), & Zhang et al. 2026 (PMID:41661604)
assessment: Non-PD executive trials and observational cohorts are null or directly conflicting across endpoints.
Older-adult 4-arm crossover (n=22) showed null postural-control and functional mobility effects of decaffeinated coffee; fall counts were not measured.
PD incidence cohort provides no fall-frequency evidence.
Fox Insight PD regression (n=4,889) showed null association between coffee consumption (p=0.2364) or dosage (p=0.7292) and freezing.
Uncontrolled PD series reported 100 mg/d caffeine eased total-akinesia FOG with reversible tolerance; abstract-only uncontrolled reporting limits reliability.
General UPDRS gait item was non-significant and did not separate freezing of gait.

study: Fuller et al. 2021 (PMID:33525438) & Deleu et al. 2006 (PMID:16966563)
assessment: Overall pegboard dexterity was null in Fuller 2021, while Deleu 2006 and Fagan 1988 assessed tapping latency/rate rather than fine dexterity.
Double-blind RCT (n=107) directly testing 340 mL brewed coffee vs decaf found null effects on fine manual laparoscopic dexterity (p=0.079/0.511).
Lived-experience reports note coffee can exacerbate hand shaking in some people with PD.

study: Hindmarch et al. 2000 (PMID:10823400) & Gardiner et al. 2025 (PMID:39377163)
assessment: Brewed coffee worsened LSEQ onset/time/quality (p<0.001) and 400 mg caffeine within 12 h of bedtime delayed sleep onset (Drake 2013 & Pauchon 2024 PMID:39458438 corroborate).
NEJM randomized case-crossover (n=100) showed actual caffeinated coffee reduced nightly sleep by 36 min (95% CI -47 to -25), opposing insomnia reduction.

study: Postuma et al. 2017 (PMID:28954882) & Postuma et al. 2012 (PMC3414662)
assessment: PD daytime-dosed caffeine trials showed non-significant nighttime sleep worsening in Café-PD (CIs cross 0) and null PSQI in Postuma 2012.
Decaf espresso served as a somnolence control with no voice-volume measurements.
PD incidence cohort provides no hypophonia or vocal-loudness outcome.

study: Jeon et al. 2019 (PMID:31193351) & Haskell-Ramsay et al. 2018 (PMC6213082)
assessment: Compositional HPLC and brewed-coffee trial quantification bridge caffeine capsule doses to brewed coffee.
6-week PD caffeine RCT (n=61) demonstrated statistically significant reduction in UPDRS-III rigidity (-1.01, 95% CI -2.0 to -0.7).
6-18 mo Café-PD RCT (n=118) found null total MDS-UPDRS III (-0.48 [-3.21 to 2.25]), indicating possible loss of short-term motor benefit over time.
Healthy-adult crossover (n=49) found no olfactory difference between caffeinated and decaffeinated coffee and lacked a water control or PD hyposmia sample.
Incidence cohort provides no olfactory severity data.

study: Aoun et al. 2021 (PMID:33715955) & Lima de Castro et al. 2024 (PMID:38308805)
assessment: Controlled studies found decaf coffee did not worsen blood pressure vs water or differ from regular coffee on intradialytic hypotension (p=0.539).
Supine BP/MSNA increase in 9 non-habitual drinkers did not test orthostatic standing tolerance or lightheadedness.

study: Heseltine et al. 1991 (PMID:1898434) & Nussberger et al. 1990 (PMID:1692926)
assessment: Decaf coffee lacked caffeine's postprandial pressor effect and showed null hemodynamic changes in healthy adults.

study: Aoun et al. 2021 (PMID:33715955) & van Dusseldorp & Katan 1990 (PMID:2372623)
assessment: Dialysis headache was null across coffee arms, and withdrawal headaches reflect sudden caffeine cessation rather than an intrinsic decaf pain effect.
Specialized high-CGA green-coffee decaf blend reduced acute headache ratings (p=0.03), but does not generalize to ordinary roasted decaf or chronic PD pain.
Ordinary brewed decaffeinated coffee did not reduce headache compared with water placebo (only caffeinated coffee did, p=0.0049 vs decaf).
Small young-adult Group 2 comparison (n=15) reported lower SOT composite/C5 after decaf, confounded by permitted milk/sugar additives and lacking a blinded water control.
Well-controlled 4-arm crossover in older adults (n=22) found decaffeinated coffee had no effect on standing postural sway vs placebo or no fluid.
Decaf espresso served only as a somnolence control with no facial-expression endpoints.
Incidence cohort provides no hypomimia severity data.
Community suggestions to try decaf aim to avoid caffeinated coffee tremor aggravation rather than proving decaf reduces baseline rest tremor.

study: Zhang et al. 2024 (PMID:39168304) & Lee et al. 2011 (PMID:21562258)
assessment: Decaf incidence cohort was null and preclinical EHT models did not test human rest tremor.

study: Marcus et al. 2023 (PMID:36947466) & Gabbert et al. 2023 (PMC10260917)
assessment: Daily step count (+1,058 steps/d) reflects activity volume rather than shortened stride, and Fox Insight walking/balance was null.
General UPDRS gait item was non-significant and did not isolate spatial stride length.
Null fine-motor brewed-coffee trial in surgeons provides no micrographia evidence.
PD caffeine RCT did not separate handwriting or micrographia outcomes.
Fox Insight PD regression (n=4,892) found coffee drinking (p=0.1615) and weekly dosage (p=0.7086) were unrelated to speech problems.
PD caffeine RCT did not isolate speech intelligibility.

study: Gabbert et al. 2023 (PMC10260917) & Cassani et al. 2017 (PMID:28647435)
assessment: Binary chewing/swallowing p=0.0497 with null dosage (p=0.6961) and duration (p=0.4785) likely reflects dysphagia reducing fluid intake rather than coffee improving swallowing.
Caffeine reduced LES pressure in healthy volunteers, an esophageal reflux proxy rather than Parkinson's oropharyngeal dysphagia.

study: Gleason et al. 2013 (PMID:22699886) & Park et al. 2023 (PMID:37015722)
assessment: NHANES epidemiological data and systematic review corroborate caffeine-associated OAB urgency.

study: Swithinbank et al. 2005 (PMID:15947624), Ha et al. 2025 (PMID:40105788), & Sauerbier et al. 2018 (PMC6312592)
assessment: Null crossover in 69 women, mixed 51-study review, and null PD NMSS urinary domain temper generalization to PD.

study: Wells et al. 2014 (PMID:24988515) & Bryant et al. 2002 (PMID:11979209)
assessment: Controlled OAB/continence trials demonstrated significant urinary urgency worsening with caffeinated vs decaffeinated drinks (p<0.01; p=0.002).

study: Agoston et al. 2022 (PMID:34792804) & Agoston et al. 2018 (PMID:30540255)
assessment: Both a n=181 DB RCT and a n=2,259 survey found caffeine/coffee did not increase hallucination-like experiences.
PD cross-sectional NMSS perceptual/hallucination scores were null across coffee categories.
Double-blind PD crossover (n=12) increased levodopa walking response magnitude and shortened walking latency, opposing walking-slowness worsening (abstract lacks exact CI).

study: Marinho et al. 2024 (PMID:39776822) & Waer et al. 2024 (PMID:39463442)
assessment: Controlled non-PD older/middle-aged trials showed caffeine accelerated 10-m walking speed (p=0.008; p<0.05) and TUG (p=0.002).

study: Richardson et al. 2024 (PMID:39321752), Norager et al. 2005 (PMID:16081625), & Postuma et al. 2012 (PMID:22855866)
assessment: Direct brewed-coffee mobility in older adults, elderly walking speed, and PD UPDRS gait were null, capping confidence at minimal_signal.
